title: Stale 100ms-guard doc refs survive guard-50 change (dead macros link.h:72-73, rpl_dodag.h:52)
description: After project-LICHEN-worker6-pj5e set LICHEN_TDMA_GUARD_MS=50, three stale references to the old 100ms guard remain in the C tree, out of pj5e's stated scope: (1) link.h:72 SLOT_DURATION_MS comment '(100ms guard, hash slot)' - macro has zero users (tx_queue.c defines its own SLOT_DURATION_MS); (2) link.h:73 GUARD_TIME_MS=100 'validated by ccp16.json' - dead macro (zero refs tree-wide) and ccp16.json contains no guard data at all, so both the value and the citation are false; (3) rpl_dodag.h:52 doc comment '100ms guard boundaries' in the RPL DODAG hash-assignment description. All three should be corrected or deleted (dead-macro removal preferred) so no reader can resurrect the 100ms value.
close_reason: Fixed all stale 100ms-guard refs: (1) link.h deleted dead macros SLOT_DURATION_MS (250, zero consumers - tx_queue.c defines its own via #ifndef and does not include link.h) and GUARD_TIME_MS=100 (zero refs tree-wide; ccp16.json contains no guard data); (2) rpl_dodag.h:52 comment reworded 100ms->50ms guard boundaries citing spec/02a §2a.2; (3) sweep found link/Kconfig:142 LICHEN_TDMA help guard=100ms -> guard=50ms. Unrelated 100s in gnss_ag3335.c, l2/*, kiss_transport.h left alone per scope. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only passes for link.h+rpl_dodag.h consumer TU, tdma.c, link_ctx.c, tx_queue.c (stub zephyr/sys/util.h, -DCONFIG_LICHEN_TDMA); rg for guard-100 patterns in link/ and rpl/ returns zero matches.
